summary.text: An indicator function of a subset maps each element of the subset to one and every other element to zero.
It has several notations, including 𝟙_A, χ_A and the Iverson bracket [ x ∈ A ].
In probability, the indicator random variable of an event A equals 1 when the outcome is in A and 0 otherwise.

facts.label: Values
facts.value: Only 1 for members and 0 for non-members

facts.label: Famous example
facts.value: The Dirichlet function is the indicator of the rationals

facts.label: Empty set
facts.value: If A is empty, its indicator is always 0

facts.label: Fuzzy sets
facts.value: Values may fall anywhere from 0 to 1

items.prompt: Let A be the set of days it rained last month. The indicator of A gives 0 for Tuesday. What does that tell you?

options.label: It rained on Tuesday
Tuesday was a day with no rain
Tuesday is not a valid day
Rain on Tuesday was unlikely

items.explain: An indicator gives one for elements of the set and zero for all others, so zero means Tuesday is not in A.

items.prompt: Suppose no element at all belongs to the set A. What does the indicator of A output?

options.label: Always 1
It is undefined
Always 0
1 for the first element and 0 after

items.explain: If A is empty, its indicator is identically zero.

items.prompt: You roll a die and let A be the event of a six. What values can the indicator random variable of A take?

options.label: The number of sixes divided by the number of rolls
The chance of getting a six
6 if a six comes up and 0 otherwise
1 if a six comes up and 0 otherwise

items.explain: The indicator random variable is 1 when the outcome is in the event and 0 otherwise.

items.prompt: A thermostat app wants to say a room is warm to a degree of 0.7, not just yes or no. Why can an ordinary indicator not do this?

options.label: It takes only the values 1 and 0, and degrees need fuzzy-set membership functions
It only works on numbers that are rational
It can only describe sets that have a smooth shape
It must always return the value one for a warm room

items.explain: In classical mathematics a set's indicator takes only 1 or 0. Fuzzy sets generalise it to values between 0 and 1, called membership functions.

items.prompt: Why do probability writers avoid calling this 1-or-0 function by its other name, characteristic function?

options.label: That name is only for sets of rational numbers
That name already means something unrelated in probability
That name belongs to fuzzy logic alone
That name describes a function that is never zero

items.explain: In classic probability theory, characteristic function has an unrelated meaning, so traditional probabilists use indicator function almost exclusively.

items.prompt: A function on the real numbers returns 1 at every rational number and 0 at every other real number. What is it called?

options.label: The Möbius function
A membership function
A dummy variable
The Dirichlet function

items.explain: The Dirichlet function is the indicator function of the rational numbers as a subset of the real numbers.
